extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers interested in religion, society, and philosophy (readers of Chesterton-style apologetics/essays)
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and summarize the author's criteria for when orthodox doctrines (miracles, Trinity, divinity of Christ, etc.) promote liberty, social action, and reform versus when modern or immanent doctrines promote passivity or oppression. Suitable for analysis of theological arguments about social and political consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthodoxy resists alliance with oppression
rubrics_metrics.description: There is only one thing that can never go past a certain point in its alliance with oppression -- and that is orthodoxy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orthodoxy can be twisted but cannot wholly justify tyranny the way certain modern doctrines can; it is uniquely limited in how far it can ally with oppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belief in miracles aligns with true liberalism
rubrics_metrics.description: In so far as the liberal idea of freedom can be said to be on either side in the discussion about miracles, it is obviously on the side of miracles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Miracles symbolize the 'liberty of God' and the 'freedom of the soul' and thus support reform and human triumph over circumstance; denying miracles often stems from materialist dogma rather than genuine liberal openness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miracles indicate human and divine liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: A miracle simply means the swift control of matter by mind; a holiday, like Liberalism, only means the liberty of man. A miracle only means the liberty of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one values human liberty and the possibility of overcoming circumstance, belief in miracles is consistent with that value even if one denies particular miracle claims as unlikely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immanence/pantheism fosters introspection and social indifference
rubrics_metrics.description: By insisting specially on the immanence of God we get introspection, self-isolation, quietism, social indifference--Tibet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The modern attitude of immanence (pantheism/theosophy) tends to encourage contentment and withdrawal from social and political action rather than reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcendence fosters wonder, vigilance, and political action
rubrics_metrics.description: By insisting specially on the transcendence of God we get wonder, curiosity, moral and political adventure, righteous indignation--Christendom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A transcendent conception of God encourages external vigilance ('WATCH and pray') and fuels the social energies that dethrone tyrants and pursue reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religions differ in teaching, not merely in outward form
rubrics_metrics.description: The religions of the earth do not greatly differ in rites and forms; they do greatly differ in what they teach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate creeds by their substantive doctrines and aims (their souls), not by their shared institutional machinery (priests, scriptures, feasts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personality and separation are prerequisites for genuine love and sociality
rubrics_metrics.description: I want to love my neighbour not because he is I, but precisely because he is not I. If souls are separate love is possible. If souls are united love is obviously impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The idea of distinct persons (as in Christianity) enables love, moral relations, and social reform; doctrines that collapse individuality (pantheism) undermine these.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trinitarian theology supports social variety and liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: To us Trinitarians--to us God Himself is a society... this triple enigma is as comforting as wine and open as an English fireside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complex, social image of God (Trinity) cultivates social instincts and balance; a solitary absolute unity (pure monotheism/Unitarians) is more likely to yield lonely, autocratic conceptions of the divine and worldly tyranny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasizing the danger of perdition motivates moral and political activity
rubrics_metrics.description: To hope for all souls is imperative; and it is quite tenable that their salvation is inevitable. ... To say that all will be well anyhow is a comprehensible remark: but it cannot be called the blast of a trumpet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stress on possible damnation or peril (original sin, hell) creates urgency ('the instant') and spurs active reform and vigilance; complacent assurances reduce impetus for change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free-will (active choice) is central to moral reform and exciting narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: A story is exciting because it has in it so strong an element of will, of what theology calls free-will... The fallacy of treating crime as disease is that evil is a matter of active choice whereas disease is not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral responsibility requires active impatience and effort (not passivity); social policies that treat sin/crime as passive disease mistake the nature of moral reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divinity that includes divine revolt/weakness empowers insurgents
rubrics_metrics.description: Christianity alone has felt that God, to be wholly God, must have been a rebel as well as a king... the author of all things went not only through agony, but through doubt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A theology in which God experienced vulnerability (e.g., Christ forsaken on the cross) legitimates human rebellion and courage; no other creed supplies a god who has 'been in revolt.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed rules and clear dogmas can protect the poor and disadvantaged
rubrics_metrics.description: If we wish to protect the poor we shall be in favour of fixed rules and clear dogmas. The RULES of a club are occasionally in favour of the poor member. The drift of a club is always in favour of the rich one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stable institutions and doctrines create predictable protections that can favor less powerful members; excessive doctrinal drift or vagueness tends to advantage the already powerful.

rubrics_metrics.name: You cannot safely extract 'the kernel' and discard the doctrines
rubrics_metrics.description: Why cannot you simply take what is good in Christianity, what you can define as valuable, what you can comprehend, and leave all the rest, all the absolute dogmas that are in their nature incomprehensible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practical social and moral fruits attributed to orthodoxy depend on its doctrines; trying to retain only selected useful elements while discarding the 'nut' (doctrinal shell) risks losing the very structures that produced those benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-orthodox agitation often destroys the very secular goods it claims to serve
rubrics_metrics.description: Men who begin to fight the Church for the sake of freedom and humanity end by flinging away freedom and humanity if only they may fight the Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Radical attacks on orthodoxy frequently undermine civil courage, political order, and social reform; opponents may wreck 'secular things' even if divine things remain intact.
